method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); the rules in one module and the party's questions in a seat module importing it; one regulative rule (s 26(2)) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seat: the party: the individual who is a party to a civil proceeding in the Supreme, County or Magistrates' Court of Victoria, bringing a claim (injured person, worker, claimant, beneficiary, employee) or answering one (cpa-seat.l4); the s 10 question can also be asked by an individual witness, expert witness or helper of a party

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: Focus: overarching purpose and obligations, certification on commencement, case management, discovery, summary judgment, expert evidence. In: ss 3 (civil proceeding, court, overarching obligations, substantive document), 4, 10 (with ss 16-26 as the obligations it applies), 18, 19, 22, 23, 26 (and s 26(2) as a regulative rule), 27, 29, 30, 31, 41, 42, 44, 45, 51, 55A(4), (5), 56, 57, 60-64, 65G, 65J(4), 65L(6), 65N, 65O, 65P(1), (4), 66(2), 67; ss 28 and 46 in descriptions. Out: ss 1, 2, 5, 6 (machinery); ss 7-9 (the purpose and the court's regard: no fact test); ss 11-15 (reach, priority, lawyers' duties); ss 16, 17, 20, 21, 24, 25 as questions of their own (standards judged by the court); ss 47-50A, 52, 53 (case management powers); ss 54, 55, 55A(1)-(3), (6), (7), 55B, 55C, 58, 59 (discovery powers); s 65 and Part 4.5 (costs powers); ss 65F, 65H, 65I, 65J(1)-(3), 65K, 65L(1)-(5), (7), 65M, 65N(1), 65P(2), (3), 65Q (expert powers); ss 66(1), (3), 68, 69; ss 70, 71 (rules and regulations); ss 72-87 (transitional, spent). Reasons in NOTES.md.
